title: Upgrade npc_behaviors.py process_npcs_on_combat bystanders from single-comment cap to real flee, hide, or intervene responses

sections.what: Allow bystander NPCs triggered via process_npcs_on_combat in engine/npc_behaviors.py to execute real physical responses (flee, hide, alert, intervene) according to traits and relationships instead of capping non-sexual reactions to one 'comment' line.
sections.why: In engine/npc_behaviors.py, process_npcs_on_combat calls process_bystander_reactions with max_reactions=1 and restricts non-sexual combat reactions to 'comment' dialogue lines. Meanwhile, npc_behaviors already has separate flee logic (lines 583-611) that only runs on periodic ticks, leaving room bystanders passively muttering one line during active violence.
sections.how: 1. Review process_npcs_on_combat and process_bystander_reactions in engine/npc_behaviors.py.\n2. Replace the single passive 'comment' max_reactions=1 cap for combat stimuli with disposition-driven bystander reactions using existing npc_behaviors flee (lines 583-611), hide, alert/shout, and ally defense hooks (guarding against infinite cascade recursion).\n3. Add pytest coverage with peaceful bystanders fleeing armed violence and allied NPCs responding cleanly.
sections.verify: 1. Run pytest covering process_npcs_on_combat with 3+ co-located NPCs of varied traits (cowardly, allied, hostile), verifying multiple witnesses respond with appropriate state changes rather than stopping at 1 passive comment.

acceptance.text: process_npcs_on_combat / process_bystander_reactions no longer limits non-sexual combat bystanders strictly to passive 'comment' text capped at max_reactions=1 across an entire crowd.
Non-combatant bystanders can react physically by disposition and fear posture (fleeing, taking cover/hiding, raising alarm, or aiding allies) using existing movement/hiding/combat helpers.

custom.browser_ui:
Intended UI home: Event Stream turn log during multi-NPC combat.

Current availability: engine/npc_behaviors.py (process_npcs_on_combat -> process_bystander_reactions) restricts non-sexual bystander combat reactions to 'comment' with max_reactions=1.

Manual verification steps:
1. Start a fight in an area containing multiple bystander NPCs (e.g. fearful civilian + brave ally).
2. Execute an attack and inspect logs and area occupancy.
   - expected: Fearful bystanders can flee or hide rather than watching passively, allies can move to intervene, and multiple witnesses are not blocked by a 1-comment cap.
